utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We were due to have evidence by the videolink this morning, and I see that in fact it is now in operation and, therefore, is effectively part of the court. I see the witness is there, and we'll deal with the situation as it now arises. We had a report earlier - why we sit late - that the accused was unwell. We now have a report from the doctor to the effect that his blood pressure is increased. A consultation with the cardiologist is recommended, together with rest for a few days. Effectively, in the absence of the accused, it will be impossible to hold the hearing, the whole purpose being for him to cross-examine the witness. Mr. Nice, if there's anything you want to say about it, of course we'll hear you, and we'll also hear from the amicus if there's anything they want to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm alarmed to hear that it's a few days that are required. I've spoken via the video-conference link with the witness, General Marinovic, this morning, and I think he's hearing what I'm saying now. He was certainly in a position to attend on a later date this week were it possible to have taken his evidence via video-conference link this week. I hadn't asked him about his availability on any later date, and indeed I don't know what difficulties there may be with keeping the videolink equipment in Dubrovnik beyond today, tomorrow, or Thursday. It may be that it would be appropriate for Your Honour to ask the witness that, not least to establish contact between the Court and the witness, the witness having made the efforts he has to be available to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, the position is simply this: I am afraid we can't go on. The accused is unwell, and the witness will have heard it, and I'm sorry that he's been troubled in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What I was suggesting is that we can ask him now whether he might be available next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you want to ask him, do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. General Marinovic, can you hear me? He has a language assistant with him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can you help us just with this --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If by chance it's not possible for your evidence to be taken this week, would you be in a position to assist next week?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As it's in the cause of justice, I am available to you every day, although it is difficult for me to give you any guarantees with respect to my health.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Nothing else I can say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Plainly the Court can't conduct proceedings in the absence of the accused. The issue we'd like to raise is really what is left of this week and the timetable, because we have to consider how we spend our time. This week was a week where we were not sitting on Friday, and the indications, from what we have heard, it being a few days of illness that is expected, is there really any prospect of this case sitting again this week?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, at the moment we can't tell you that. The answer we have is rest for a few days and a consultation with the cardiologist. I suggest the best course is that we will assess the situation as soon as we can. On the other hand, if it's possible to sit later in the week, we should most certainly take that opportunity and not lose time. So we will let you know as soon as we can if we're not going to sit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That was all I was really concerned with was that information gets passed to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber will do this: We will ask for a full medical report and for the cardiologist to report, if he can, tomorrow. We will then be in a position to reassess the situation for the rest of the week. General, I'm sorry, as I've said, that you've had to come and that we haven't been able to take your evidence and indeed that the equipment was not ready, as it should have been, yesterday. But we will rearrange your evidence at a later date, and if you would stay in touch, please, with the Court. We will try and fix a hearing which is convenient to you and convenient to the Court too. I'm going to deal with one other matter. I don't think it need concern you. It's purely an administrative matter. It's this: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, you are -- thank you for coming in. Just to deal with the remainder of the 92 bis witnesses who we've got to consider, we will consider at the first opportunity, first of all the transcript witnesses relating to Vukovar. There are seven of those. We will then deal with the witnesses, as it were, from the periphery. I'm just talking geographically: Baranja, Bacin, Saborsko, Lipovaca and Bruska. I should say the witness can go, of course, if he wants, at the end of the videolink. No need for him to remain. There are about 14 or 15 witnesses there. I was going to ask you this: You've had a chance to reconsider, in order to save time and indeed to make our consideration that much more efficient. Are there any witnesses on the list who you no longer intend to call?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have -- we had already addressed the witness Stringer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And I have said that we don't want to call this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: But in relation to the peripheral witnesses, there's actually just one witness per village, more or less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And we would -- we will reconsider it, but it's not very likely that we can drop any of these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: But of course when we have your decision on the 92 bis, whether it is with cross-examination or not, then we, of course, need to think about it in a different way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nice, unless there's anything else we can usefully do, we will adjourn and give notice as soon as we can when the Court will next reconvene.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Two things. First, just notice which will be on the transcript so the accused can read it: I said yesterday we would not be calling 97. There has been some reconsideration. It remains possible that we will him. I'll keep you posted on that. Secondly, we were looking at the possibility of a gap in this week's schedule because of the problems with the videolink and the disappearance from the list of the man originally listed as a witness for today. I should tell the Chamber that we face this problem: That the Victims and Witnesses Unit is not able to bring us witnesses at short notice, and anything less than five days is regarded as unacceptably short notice. So that when we have a gap, as it looked as though we might have a gap for reasons outside our control, and we looked for a comparatively local witness who we could bring in today to give evidence on Thursday - because that would be less than five days' notice - that was not a possibility that could be considered. I draw it to your attention. I don't seek any relief, but I desire that you should understand the difficulties that putting together the various functions of this Tribunal pose. We're doing all we can, obviously, to have enough witnesses available that there should be no gaps. If we have too many witnesses available we fall foul of the complaint that we're wasting their time and spending very large quantities of money. It's a difficult balancing exercise. As for myself, I have a personal commitment on Thursday. I'll tell you through your officers what it is. I think I'm satisfied that I will in fact put the interests of being here above that other commitment, but nevertheless, it will help me to know tomorrow, if it's possible, whether we're going to be sitting on Thursday. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, how are the five days' notice explained? I of course accept what you say, but just for my own information.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If we seek to call a witness without giving five days' notice, VWU cannot do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to have explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm afraid I can't explain it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You can't. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: But they have an enormous workload to serve a large number of courts, and limited staff. I can't speak for them, I can only report what the position facing us is. And the only way we can possibly occasionally get round that is if we circumvent the VWU arrangements and bring a witness in under our own system, but that, I think, brings in all sorts of other difficulties of one kind or another and is also really contrary to the principle of the Tribunal that victims and witnesses are handled by an independent unit, which brings many advantages for the Court and for the witnesses. That's the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We will adjourn and we will sit at a date which will be notified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: at 9.53 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned sine die
